column3: Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew begins with the gates not being opened, using the passive; BSB says “Do not open” them. The Hebrew refers to those standing by a pronoun; BSB explicitly names the guards.
The Hebrew uses the image of being broad of hands for the city’s spaciousness; BSB says spacious.
The Hebrew describes those who went up at first; BSB describes those who first returned.
The Hebrew calls these people sons of the province and explicitly names Babylon as the king’s realm; BSB says people of the province and “its king.”
